title: Creation and Annihilation
notes: Pair Production: A high-energy photon (gamma ray) converts into an electron-positron pair near a nucleus: γ + nucleus → e⁻ + e⁺ + nucleus. The nucleus recoils to conserve momentum. Threshold energy: E_γ ≥ 2m_ec² = 1.022 MeV.

Pair Annihilation: An electron and positron collide and convert to photons: e⁻ + e⁺ → 2γ. Each photon has energy m_ec² = 0.511 MeV (if at rest), emitted in opposite directions (180° apart) to conserve momentum.
Energy Conservation: In pair production, photon energy = 2m_ec² + kinetic energies of pair + recoil of nucleus. In annihilation, total energy (rest + kinetic) converts to photon energy.
Momentum Conservation: A photon cannot produce an e⁻e⁺ pair in empty space — momentum cannot be conserved. A nearby nucleus (or electron) absorbs recoil momentum.
Charge Conservation: Pair production creates net charge 0 (−e + +e = 0); annihilation starts with net charge 0. Charge is conserved.

Applications: PET scans (positron emission tomography) use annihilation photons (511 keV each, back-to-back) for medical imaging. Positrons from radioactive tracers annihilate with electrons in tissue.
Matter-Antimatter Asymmetry: Universe appears dominated by matter with very little antimatter — one of the great unsolved problems in physics (baryon asymmetry).

specificConditions: Threshold Energy: Pair production requires photon energy ≥ 1.022 MeV (2 × electron rest energy). Below threshold, no pair creation.
Third Body Required: Pair production cannot occur in vacuum — needs nucleus/electron to conserve momentum.
Photon Disappears: In pair production, the photon is completely absorbed — it does not survive.
formulas: Annihilation photon energy: E_γ = m_ec² = 0.511 MeV (each, at rest)
Momentum conservation: p_photon = p_e⁻ + p_e⁺ + p_recoil
keyPoints: Pair production: γ → e⁻ + e⁺, needs E ≥ 1.022 MeV, needs nucleus.
Annihilation: e⁻ + e⁺ → 2γ, each photon 0.511 MeV (at rest).
Nucleus needed for momentum conservation in pair production.
PET scans use 511 keV annihilation photons for medical imaging.
Energy and momentum both conserved in creation/annihilation.
importantNotes: The photon disappears completely in pair production — all its energy goes into creating mass and kinetic energy.
In annihilation at rest, two 0.511 MeV photons go in exactly opposite directions (180°).
PET scan detection: coincident detection of two 511 keV photons localizes the annihilation point.
Antimatter (positron) is rare in the universe — created in cosmic rays, radioactive decay, particle accelerators.
examShortTricks: Annihilation photons: 0.511 MeV each, opposite directions.
Need nucleus for pair production (momentum conservation).
PET: 511 keV photons detected in coincidence.
examNotes: NEB frequently asks to describe pair production and annihilation with energy thresholds.

PET scan application is a common real-world example.
examples: Photon of 1.5 MeV produces e⁻e⁺ pair. Excess energy = 1.5 - 1.022 = 0.478 MeV shared as kinetic energy of pair and nuclear recoil.
Positron emitted in tissue annihilates with electron. Two 511 keV photons travel back-to-back — detected by PET scanner ring.
Electron and positron each with kinetic energy 0.1 MeV annihilate: Total photon energy = 2(0.511 + 0.1) = 1.222 MeV shared between two photons.

universalFacts: Positron was predicted by Dirac (1928) and discovered by Anderson (1932) in cosmic rays.
Every particle has an antiparticle with same mass but opposite charge — predicted by quantum field theory.
The observable universe has matter-antimatter asymmetry — why matter dominates is unsolved.
Antimatter is used in PET scans and studied at CERN (antihydrogen trapping).
confusion: Thinking pair production can happen in empty space: Momentum conservation forbids it — need nucleus.
Believing annihilation produces one photon: Two photons needed for momentum conservation (at rest).
Confusing positron with proton: Positron = +e, same mass as electron; proton = +e, ~1836× electron mass.
Thinking photon survives in pair production: Photon is fully absorbed/converted.
Believing matter and antimatter are equally common: Universe is overwhelmingly matter.

summary: Pair production (γ → e⁻ + e⁺, E ≥ 1.022 MeV) and annihilation (e⁻ + e⁺ → 2γ, 0.511 MeV each) demonstrate mass-energy conversion. A nucleus is needed for momentum conservation in production. PET scans use annihilation photons for medical imaging.
